content.user_title: Build Rust Test Mocks with Trait Patterns
content.value_statement: Rust tests often become slow or fragile when they depend on databases, HTTP services, or real infrastructure. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design trait-based mocks, controlled failures, and fixture helpers.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to introduce trait-based mocks for external dependencies.
Shows simple mock repositories for async Rust service tests.
Demonstrates verification of side effects such as sent email records.
Provides patterns for controlled success, not-found, and database-error behavior.
Outlines in-memory repositories and fixture helpers for repeatable tests.
limitations: Focuses on Rust examples and does not cover every mocking framework.
Does not run tests or inspect project code without user-provided context.
Assumes the project can introduce traits around external dependencies.
Provides guidance, not a complete test suite for an application.

use_cases.title: Mock a Repository
use_cases.description: Design a lightweight repository mock for a Rust service that depends on stored user data.

use_cases.title: Verify Side Effects
use_cases.description: Capture calls to an email or notification service and assert that the service behaved correctly.

use_cases.title: Remove Infrastructure From Tests
use_cases.description: Replace database or HTTP dependencies with trait abstractions and in-memory test implementations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Mock
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple test double.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a simple Rust mock for a trait-based repository. Explain the structure and the test flow.

prompt_templates.title: Add Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to assert side effects.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to design a mock service that records calls so my Rust test can verify side effects.

prompt_templates.title: Model Failure Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for success and error behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust mock strategy that can return success, not-found, and database-error outcomes for service tests.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Testability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust service design and suggest trait boundaries, mock implementations, and fixture helpers for maintainable tests.

output_examples.input: I need to test a service that reads users from a repository.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest a trait-backed mock repository, seeded test users, and assertions around successful and missing-user paths.

output_examples.input: I need to verify that registration sends a welcome email.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a mock email service that records sent messages, then checks the recipient count and subject intent.

output_examples.input: My unit tests depend on a real database.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest extracting a repository trait and replacing the database with an in-memory implementation for unit tests.

best_practices: Keep mocks small and local to the behavior under test.
Model expected failures explicitly so tests check error handling.
Use fixture helpers for shared data, but keep assertions in the test body.
anti_patterns: Using production databases or HTTP services for unit tests.
Coupling service logic directly to concrete infrastructure clients.
Writing mocks that hide important errors or accept every input.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design Rust mock implementations, in-memory repositories, and fixture helpers for tests around external dependencies.

faq.question: Does it execute test commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation only and declares Read and Grep as allowed tools.

faq.question: Does it require a mocking framework?
faq.answer: No. The examples focus on hand-written trait implementations that are easy to understand and adjust.

faq.question: Can it help with async Rust tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show async trait implementations and service tests that use asynchronous calls.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I avoid this pattern?
faq.answer: Avoid it when an integration test needs real database behavior, network behavior, or framework-specific guarantees.
